chapter: Willie Lynch, the Blue Rhythm Band and Teddy Hill
title: Doubling on clarinet and Howard Johnson and Chu Berry replacing him
summary: He carried clarinet and soprano in one case, had given up baritone, and left Hill's band when Johnson and Chu Berry came in.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Now, you mentioned that Blanchard played violin. Did he do any of that with Teddy Hill?
No. He didn't touch the violin with Teddy. Yeah, he was a great violinist. But he didn't play it with Teddy Hill. He played clarinet and saxophone.
At this point you were still doubling clarinet?
Well, I was carrying it around -- and my soprano saxophone. The three of them fit in the case.
What about a baritone? You weren't playing any baritone.
No, no, I got rid of that. Too big for me.
Did Teddy Hill double on baritone or bass sax?
But he doubled on clarinet, did he?
Well, everybody had a clarinet. If they had them. Some of them wish they hadn't had them. Yeah,
And then do you remember that Howard Johnson replaced you, and Chu Berry came in at about the same time.
Yeah, well, that was a little later when both of them were in there.
That's when you went out, probably back to Russell.

That's right. Because at that time, Teddy's band changed completely, when Chu Berry come in the band, and I think Bill Dillard... I don't know if Bill Dillard was there when I was there or not . I worked with Bill so many places. He could have been in Teddy's band when I was working with Blanchard.
